items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1965-09-13
items.q: Fasola was about, well, when I was playing there, Fasola was a little younger than me. And you talk about something funny. He used to come around in short pants.

ctx.x: Right. I said, I said, Harry Shields was playing clarinet. Bill replaced Harry later on. That's right. Now, the point is this, Charlie, that in this place, all the musicians used to drop in, you see, because it was a meeting place. Shawky used to stop in there. Fasola. Fasola was about, well, when I was playing there, Fasola was a little younger than me. And you talk about something funny. He used to come around in short pants. And he weighed about, he weighed about 200 pounds with short pants and a cap. There…
I'm sorry, before you go on, did you mention the name of this place?

items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: Fazz was playing third sax, I believe, in those days.

ctx.x: What would they play? Did you play both?

Well, let's see. I think Gene Meyer was playing, or Meyer Weinboy was playing alto lead. Fazz was playing third sax, I believe, in those days. And Scagliona was playing tenor, if I'm not mistaken. That was a real good band. And Joe Lloyd Cannon was playing bass. Aubrey Schlang played drums. That was a real good spot.
How did that deal work there? Who would have the band in charge? Shawkey.
